audit.title: CCIP Best Practices (EVM)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Most sections open with the actionable claim, e.g. "If `extraArgs` are left empty, a default of *200000* `gasLimit` will be set." A few sections ("Evaluate the security…") open with hedged prose that doesn't state the practice crisply.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Clean H2→H4 hierarchy, median 47 words/section, 0 sections over 600 words. Weakness: **0 tables** — role permissions and the `allowOutOfOrderExecution` Optional/Required matrix are prose/bullets where a table would extract far better.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Mixed. Good specifics exist (200000 default gasLimit, 8 vs 18 decimals, `10^10` scaling, 50%/30% thresholds) but the facts block flags **0 numerals with units** and vague quantifiers ("various", "most"). Deprecation "early 2026" is imprecise.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; links to Ethereum execution-apis, Foundry, Hedera docs, and GitHub source. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good — "The **token admin** is responsible for configuring token pools across blockchains…" is liftable. Some roles (rebalancer, rate limit admin) defined; CCIP itself is not defined on-page for a cold reader.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `datePublished`/`dateModified`, no og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>`. This is largely a site-template fix but directly lowers agent trust/E-E-A-T signals.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak for the format — 1 fenced block, untagged, non-runnable (`Scaled Fee = getFee() * 10^10`). This is a prose best-practices page so low code is expected, but the one block should be language-tagged and the Hedera example would benefit from a real snippet.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Fair. Broad lifecycle coverage (verify → gas → liquidity → monitor → chain-specific), but headings are concept-named, not question/symptom-named; no FAQ or troubleshooting framing for error strings devs actually paste.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong and consistent. One rendering glitch: `\*\* Delegate Rate Limit Admin Role \*\*` shows broken bold markup.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured, action-oriented best-practices reference for building on CCIP over EVM chains, strong on internal cross-linking (18 internal, 14 external, 3 primary-source links) and clean sectioning (37 headings, 0 level skips, 0 oversized sections). Its biggest GEO strength is chunkability: nearly every section is a self-contained retrievable unit. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability — the served HTML carries **no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no schema dates** despite a visible "Last Updated: 2025-05-19" — compounded by concept-titled (not symptom-titled) headings that miss the way developers actually query. Honest verdict: solid, agent-friendly content undermined by missing structured metadata and query-phrasing gaps that cost retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: Section headings throughout; new "FAQ / Troubleshooting" H2 near the end.
recommendations.issue: Concept titles like "Verify sender", "Using `extraArgs`" miss "how do I…" and error-string queries.
recommendations.change: Add question-form subheadings or FAQ entries: "Why did my CCIP message revert on a Required out-of-order lane?", "Why is my Hedera fee 10^10 too small?", "How do I estimate gasLimit for ccipReceive?". Keep the answer in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical URL and dates
recommendations.issue: Facts show 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, dateModified absent despite visible "Last Updated: 2025-05-19".
recommendations.change: Add a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referencing `canonical`. Surface the last-updated date in structured markup, not just body text.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Convert role permissions to a comparison table
recommendations.issue: token admin, token pool owner, rate limit admin, rebalancer defined across scattered bullets; 0 tables on page.
recommendations.change: Add a table: Role | Can do | Assign to | Function(s) (e.g. `setRateLimitAdmin()`, `provideLiquidity`).
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract discrete role→permission reasons and build justified answers.

recommendations.title: Tabulate the `allowOutOfOrderExecution` decision matrix
recommendations.issue: Optional/Required × true/false logic is nested bullets, easy to mis-synthesize.
recommendations.change: Table: Lane property (Optional/Required) | Allowed values | Behavior | Reverts? Lead with the canonical rule "On Required lanes you **must** set `true`."
recommendations.why: Reduces the chance an engine inverts the Required-lane rule — a high-severity error.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers and add units/precision
recommendations.where: "Ensure Sufficient Liquidity" ("various threshold levels"); deprecation note "early 2026".
recommendations.issue: Facts flag vague quantifiers and 0 numerals with units.
recommendations.change: State thresholds numerically inline (already partly done: 50%/30%); give the deprecation a concrete quarter/date if known; add units to gas figures ("200000 gas units").
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Tag and complete the one code block; add a runnable Hedera snippet
recommendations.issue: Untagged block `Scaled Fee = getFee() * 10^10` is pseudocode, not runnable.
recommendations.change: Tag as `text` or provide a `javascript`/`solidity` snippet: `const scaledFee = fee * 10n ** 10n;` with the `ccipSend` `msg.value` usage.
recommendations.why: Copy-pasteable, language-labeled code is preferentially cited by coding agents.

recommendations.title: Fix broken bold markup
recommendations.where: "Best Practices for Token Pool Owners…" bullet.
recommendations.issue: `\*\* Delegate Rate Limit Admin Role \*\*` renders literally.
recommendations.change: Correct to `**Delegate Rate Limit Admin Role**`.
recommendations.why: Clean presentation is independently rewarded by engines.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers ("various threshold levels", "most EVM chains") — minor.
One untagged, non-runnable fenced code block.
Broken markdown emphasis on the "Delegate Rate Limit Admin Role" bullet.
No stale-content issue: "Last Updated: 2025-05-19" is present in body (but not in schema).
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and og/date tags are almost certainly controlled by the site template — fix once at the layout level to benefit all docs pages.
The page already references `/llms.txt`; ensure this page is listed there so agents can discover it.
CLI should pass raw `<head>` on future runs — head metadata could not be verified here, so the metadata score reflects served-HTML absence, not confirmed omission.
